title: Correct one rule inside an existing skill without forking or truncating it
intent: The update-in-place rail, ported to skills: a write with no item_id creates a SECOND skill, and two skills covering the same ground both get injected by skills_context, so the agent that reads them is handed a contradiction. The second half is carry-forward — item_id alone is a REPLACE (store.py:118), so a model that sends only the corrected section silently deletes the other four rules while its own report says it fixed the threshold. The skill body is longer than the 700-char window skills_context injects (memory.py:29), so the whole document is only knowable through read_memory_item.
prompt: The 'Refreshing a Stale Topic' skill has the staleness threshold wrong — it says 30 days and it should be 90. Fix that. Everything else in there is right, so leave it exactly as it is.

source_facts: The skill is skills/refreshing-a-stale-topic.md, five numbered rules, written 2026-07-19.
Rule 1 currently says a topic is stale when its frontmatter timestamp is more than 30 days old. The operator says 90.

Rule 2 (refresh in place with item_id, no item_id creates a second topic, the Kimi K3 note twice), rule 3 (carry forward what the new source does not contradict), rule 4 (report the diff — old value, new value, and what stayed the same) and rule 5 (do not refresh when the source_url 404s, is parked, or has changed subject) are all correct and must survive unchanged.
write_memory with item_id and neither append nor prepend REPLACES the body (store.py:118). The content argument is therefore the whole corrected document, not the delta.
The frontmatter description, tags and category are preserved automatically by write_concept's merge (store.py:106) and do not need re-supplying.
traps: Writing with no item_id, which creates a second skill with a near-identical slug. Both are then retrievable and they disagree about the threshold.

Sending only the corrected rule 1 as the content of a replace, which deletes rules 2 through 5. The agent's report says the threshold is fixed and it is — in a document that no longer says anything else.
Using append=true to bolt a corrected rule 1 onto the end, which leaves the wrong 30-day rule in the body above it. Two thresholds in one skill is worse than the wrong one alone.
Leaving '30 days' in as a parenthetical history note ('previously 30 days'). A skill is read and followed, not studied — another agent handed both numbers has to guess.
Answering without reading the item first, and reconstructing the other four rules from the 700-char snippet in the prompt, which is truncated.
judge.guidance: carry_forward is the primary dimension: check every one of rules 2 through 5 is present in the stored body with its specifics intact (item_id, the Kimi K3 incident, 'does not contradict', the 404/parked-domain case). Score change_reporting on naming the old and new values rather than saying the skill was updated. Conciseness is a tiebreak — this is one read and one write.
